scene.label: Act 1, Scene 1
scene.title: SCENE I. A hall in the Duke's palace
scene.location: A hall in the Duke's palace

content.text: Enter Duke, Egeon, Jailer, Officers and other Attendants.

lines.text: Proceed, Solinus, to procure my fall,
lines.plainText: Proceed Solinus to procure my fall

lines.text: And by the doom of death end woes and all.
lines.plainText: And by the doom of death end woes and all

lines.text: Merchant of Syracusa, plead no more.
lines.plainText: Merchant of Syracusa plead no more

lines.text: I am not partial to infringe our laws.
lines.plainText: I am not partial to infringe our laws

lines.text: The enmity and discord which of late
lines.plainText: The enmity and discord which of late

lines.text: Sprung from the rancorous outrage of your Duke
lines.plainText: Sprung from the rancorous outrage of your Duke

lines.text: To merchants, our well-dealing countrymen,
lines.plainText: To merchants our welldealing countrymen

lines.text: Who, wanting guilders to redeem their lives,
lines.plainText: Who wanting guilders to redeem their lives

lines.text: Have seal'd his rigorous statutes with their bloods,
lines.plainText: Have seal'd his rigorous statutes with their bloods

lines.text: Excludes all pity from our threat'ning looks.
lines.plainText: Excludes all pity from our threat'ning looks

lines.text: For since the mortal and intestine jars
lines.plainText: For since the mortal and intestine jars

lines.text: 'Twixt thy seditious countrymen and us,
lines.plainText: 'Twixt thy seditious countrymen and us

lines.text: It hath in solemn synods been decreed,
lines.plainText: It hath in solemn synods been decreed

lines.text: Both by the Syracusians and ourselves,
lines.plainText: Both by the Syracusians and ourselves

lines.text: To admit no traffic to our adverse towns;
lines.plainText: To admit no traffic to our adverse towns

lines.text: Nay more, if any born at Ephesus
lines.plainText: Nay more if any born at Ephesus

lines.text: Be seen at Syracusian marts and fairs;
lines.plainText: Be seen at Syracusian marts and fairs

lines.text: Again, if any Syracusian born
lines.plainText: Again if any Syracusian born

lines.text: Come to the bay of Ephesus, he dies,
lines.plainText: Come to the bay of Ephesus he dies

lines.text: His goods confiscate to the Duke's dispose,
lines.plainText: His goods confiscate to the Duke's dispose

lines.text: Unless a thousand marks be levied
lines.plainText: Unless a thousand marks be levied

lines.text: To quit the penalty and to ransom him.
lines.plainText: To quit the penalty and to ransom him

lines.text: Thy substance, valued at the highest rate,
lines.plainText: Thy substance valued at the highest rate

lines.text: Cannot amount unto a hundred marks;
lines.plainText: Cannot amount unto a hundred marks

lines.text: Therefore by law thou art condemn'd to die.
lines.plainText: Therefore by law thou art condemn'd to die

lines.text: Yet this my comfort; when your words are done,
lines.plainText: Yet this my comfort when your words are done

lines.text: My woes end likewise with the evening sun.
lines.plainText: My woes end likewise with the evening sun

lines.text: Well, Syracusian, say in brief the cause
lines.plainText: Well Syracusian say in brief the cause

lines.text: Why thou departedst from thy native home,
lines.plainText: Why thou departedst from thy native home

lines.text: And for what cause thou cam'st to Ephesus.
lines.plainText: And for what cause thou cam'st to Ephesus

lines.text: A heavier task could not have been impos'd
lines.plainText: A heavier task could not have been impos'd

lines.text: Than I to speak my griefs unspeakable;
lines.plainText: Than I to speak my griefs unspeakable

lines.text: Yet, that the world may witness that my end
lines.plainText: Yet that the world may witness that my end

lines.text: Was wrought by nature, not by vile offence,
lines.plainText: Was wrought by nature not by vile offence

lines.text: I'll utter what my sorrow gives me leave.
lines.plainText: I'll utter what my sorrow gives me leave

lines.text: In Syracusa was I born, and wed
lines.plainText: In Syracusa was I born and wed

lines.text: Unto a woman happy but for me,
lines.plainText: Unto a woman happy but for me

lines.text: And by me, had not our hap been bad.
lines.plainText: And by me had not our hap been bad

lines.text: With her I liv'd in joy; our wealth increas'd
lines.plainText: With her I liv'd in joy our wealth increas'd

lines.text: By prosperous voyages I often made
lines.plainText: By prosperous voyages I often made

lines.text: To Epidamnum, till my factor's death,
lines.plainText: To Epidamnum till my factor's death

lines.text: And the great care of goods at random left,
lines.plainText: And the great care of goods at random left

lines.text: Drew me from kind embracements of my spouse;
lines.plainText: Drew me from kind embracements of my spouse

lines.text: From whom my absence was not six months old
lines.plainText: From whom my absence was not six months old

lines.text: Before herself (almost at fainting under
lines.plainText: Before herself almost at fainting under

lines.text: The pleasing punishment that women bear)
lines.plainText: The pleasing punishment that women bear

lines.text: Had made provision for her following me,
lines.plainText: Had made provision for her following me

lines.text: And soon and safe arrived where I was.
lines.plainText: And soon and safe arrived where I was

lines.text: There had she not been long but she became
lines.plainText: There had she not been long but she became

lines.text: A joyful mother of two goodly sons,
lines.plainText: A joyful mother of two goodly sons

lines.text: And, which was strange, the one so like the other
lines.plainText: And which was strange the one so like the other

lines.text: As could not be distinguish'd but by names.
lines.plainText: As could not be distinguish'd but by names

lines.text: That very hour, and in the self-same inn,
lines.plainText: That very hour and in the selfsame inn

lines.text: A mean woman was delivered
lines.plainText: A mean woman was delivered

lines.text: Of such a burden, male twins, both alike.
lines.plainText: Of such a burden male twins both alike

lines.text: Those, for their parents were exceeding poor,
lines.plainText: Those for their parents were exceeding poor

lines.text: I bought, and brought up to attend my sons.
lines.plainText: I bought and brought up to attend my sons

lines.text: My wife, not meanly proud of two such boys,
lines.plainText: My wife not meanly proud of two such boys

lines.text: Made daily motions for our home return.
lines.plainText: Made daily motions for our home return

lines.text: Unwilling I agreed; alas, too soon
lines.plainText: Unwilling I agreed alas too soon

lines.text: We came aboard.
lines.plainText: We came aboard

lines.text: A league from Epidamnum had we sail'd
lines.plainText: A league from Epidamnum had we sail'd

lines.text: Before the always-wind-obeying deep
lines.plainText: Before the alwayswindobeying deep

lines.text: Gave any tragic instance of our harm;
lines.plainText: Gave any tragic instance of our harm

lines.text: But longer did we not retain much hope;
lines.plainText: But longer did we not retain much hope

lines.text: For what obscured light the heavens did grant
lines.plainText: For what obscured light the heavens did grant

lines.text: Did but convey unto our fearful minds
lines.plainText: Did but convey unto our fearful minds

lines.text: A doubtful warrant of immediate death,
lines.plainText: A doubtful warrant of immediate death

lines.text: Which though myself would gladly have embrac'd,
lines.plainText: Which though myself would gladly have embrac'd

lines.text: Yet the incessant weepings of my wife,
lines.plainText: Yet the incessant weepings of my wife

lines.text: Weeping before for what she saw must come,
lines.plainText: Weeping before for what she saw must come

lines.text: And piteous plainings of the pretty babes,
lines.plainText: And piteous plainings of the pretty babes

lines.text: That mourn'd for fashion, ignorant what to fear,
lines.plainText: That mourn'd for fashion ignorant what to fear

lines.text: Forc'd me to seek delays for them and me.
lines.plainText: Forc'd me to seek delays for them and me

lines.text: And this it was (for other means was none).
lines.plainText: And this it was for other means was none

lines.text: The sailors sought for safety by our boat,
lines.plainText: The sailors sought for safety by our boat

lines.text: And left the ship, then sinking-ripe, to us.
lines.plainText: And left the ship then sinkingripe to us

lines.text: My wife, more careful for the latter-born,
lines.plainText: My wife more careful for the latterborn

lines.text: Had fast'ned him unto a small spare mast,
lines.plainText: Had fast'ned him unto a small spare mast

lines.text: Such as sea-faring men provide for storms.
lines.plainText: Such as seafaring men provide for storms

lines.text: To him one of the other twins was bound,
lines.plainText: To him one of the other twins was bound

lines.text: Whilst I had been like heedful of the other.
lines.plainText: Whilst I had been like heedful of the other

lines.text: The children thus dispos'd, my wife and I,
lines.plainText: The children thus dispos'd my wife and I

lines.text: Fixing our eyes on whom our care was fix'd,
lines.plainText: Fixing our eyes on whom our care was fix'd

lines.text: Fast'ned ourselves at either end the mast,
lines.plainText: Fast'ned ourselves at either end the mast

lines.text: And, floating straight, obedient to the stream,
lines.plainText: And floating straight obedient to the stream

lines.text: Was carried towards Corinth, as we thought.
lines.plainText: Was carried towards Corinth as we thought

lines.text: At length the sun, gazing upon the earth,
lines.plainText: At length the sun gazing upon the earth

lines.text: Dispers'd those vapours that offended us,
lines.plainText: Dispers'd those vapours that offended us

lines.text: And by the benefit of his wished light
lines.plainText: And by the benefit of his wished light

lines.text: The seas wax'd calm, and we discovered
lines.plainText: The seas wax'd calm and we discovered

lines.text: Two ships from far, making amain to us,
lines.plainText: Two ships from far making amain to us

lines.text: Of Corinth that, of Epidaurus this.
lines.plainText: Of Corinth that of Epidaurus this

lines.text: But ere they came—O, let me say no more!
lines.plainText: But ere they cameO let me say no more

lines.text: Gather the sequel by that went before.
lines.plainText: Gather the sequel by that went before

lines.text: Nay, forward, old man, do not break off so,
lines.plainText: Nay forward old man do not break off so

lines.text: For we may pity, though not pardon thee.
lines.plainText: For we may pity though not pardon thee

lines.text: O, had the gods done so, I had not now
lines.plainText: O had the gods done so I had not now

lines.text: Worthily term'd them merciless to us.
lines.plainText: Worthily term'd them merciless to us

lines.text: For, ere the ships could meet by twice five leagues,
lines.plainText: For ere the ships could meet by twice five leagues

lines.text: We were encountered by a mighty rock,
lines.plainText: We were encountered by a mighty rock

lines.text: Which being violently borne upon,
lines.plainText: Which being violently borne upon

lines.text: Our helpful ship was splitted in the midst;
lines.plainText: Our helpful ship was splitted in the midst

lines.text: So that, in this unjust divorce of us,
lines.plainText: So that in this unjust divorce of us

lines.text: Fortune had left to both of us alike
lines.plainText: Fortune had left to both of us alike

lines.text: What to delight in, what to sorrow for.
lines.plainText: What to delight in what to sorrow for

lines.text: Her part, poor soul, seeming as burdened
lines.plainText: Her part poor soul seeming as burdened

lines.text: With lesser weight, but not with lesser woe,
lines.plainText: With lesser weight but not with lesser woe

lines.text: Was carried with more speed before the wind,
lines.plainText: Was carried with more speed before the wind

lines.text: And in our sight they three were taken up
lines.plainText: And in our sight they three were taken up

lines.text: By fishermen of Corinth, as we thought.
lines.plainText: By fishermen of Corinth as we thought

lines.text: At length another ship had seiz'd on us;
lines.plainText: At length another ship had seiz'd on us

lines.text: And, knowing whom it was their hap to save,
lines.plainText: And knowing whom it was their hap to save

lines.text: Gave healthful welcome to their ship-wrack'd guests,
lines.plainText: Gave healthful welcome to their shipwrack'd guests

lines.text: And would have reft the fishers of their prey,
lines.plainText: And would have reft the fishers of their prey

lines.text: Had not their bark been very slow of sail;
lines.plainText: Had not their bark been very slow of sail

lines.text: And therefore homeward did they bend their course.
lines.plainText: And therefore homeward did they bend their course

lines.text: Thus have you heard me sever'd from my bliss,
lines.plainText: Thus have you heard me sever'd from my bliss

lines.text: That by misfortunes was my life prolong'd
lines.plainText: That by misfortunes was my life prolong'd

lines.text: To tell sad stories of my own mishaps.
lines.plainText: To tell sad stories of my own mishaps

lines.text: And for the sake of them thou sorrowest for,
lines.plainText: And for the sake of them thou sorrowest for

lines.text: Do me the favour to dilate at full
lines.plainText: Do me the favour to dilate at full

lines.text: What have befall'n of them and thee till now.
lines.plainText: What have befall'n of them and thee till now

lines.text: My youngest boy, and yet my eldest care,
lines.plainText: My youngest boy and yet my eldest care

lines.text: At eighteen years became inquisitive
lines.plainText: At eighteen years became inquisitive

lines.text: After his brother, and importun'd me
lines.plainText: After his brother and importun'd me

lines.text: That his attendant, so his case was like,
lines.plainText: That his attendant so his case was like

lines.text: Reft of his brother, but retain'd his name,
lines.plainText: Reft of his brother but retain'd his name

lines.text: Might bear him company in the quest of him;
lines.plainText: Might bear him company in the quest of him

lines.text: Whom whilst I laboured of a love to see,
lines.plainText: Whom whilst I laboured of a love to see

lines.text: I hazarded the loss of whom I lov'd.
lines.plainText: I hazarded the loss of whom I lov'd

lines.text: Five summers have I spent in farthest Greece,
lines.plainText: Five summers have I spent in farthest Greece

lines.text: Roaming clean through the bounds of Asia,
lines.plainText: Roaming clean through the bounds of Asia

lines.text: And, coasting homeward, came to Ephesus,
lines.plainText: And coasting homeward came to Ephesus

lines.text: Hopeless to find, yet loath to leave unsought
lines.plainText: Hopeless to find yet loath to leave unsought

lines.text: Or that or any place that harbours men.
lines.plainText: Or that or any place that harbours men

lines.text: But here must end the story of my life;
lines.plainText: But here must end the story of my life

lines.text: And happy were I in my timely death,
lines.plainText: And happy were I in my timely death

lines.text: Could all my travels warrant me they live.
lines.plainText: Could all my travels warrant me they live

lines.text: Hapless Egeon, whom the fates have mark'd
lines.plainText: Hapless Egeon whom the fates have mark'd

lines.text: To bear the extremity of dire mishap;
lines.plainText: To bear the extremity of dire mishap

lines.text: Now, trust me, were it not against our laws,
lines.plainText: Now trust me were it not against our laws

lines.text: Against my crown, my oath, my dignity,
lines.plainText: Against my crown my oath my dignity

lines.text: Which princes, would they, may not disannul,
lines.plainText: Which princes would they may not disannul

lines.text: My soul should sue as advocate for thee.
lines.plainText: My soul should sue as advocate for thee

lines.text: But though thou art adjudged to the death,
lines.plainText: But though thou art adjudged to the death

lines.text: And passed sentence may not be recall'd
lines.plainText: And passed sentence may not be recall'd

lines.text: But to our honour's great disparagement,
lines.plainText: But to our honour's great disparagement

lines.text: Yet will I favour thee in what I can.
lines.plainText: Yet will I favour thee in what I can

lines.text: Therefore, merchant, I'll limit thee this day
lines.plainText: Therefore merchant I'll limit thee this day

lines.text: To seek thy health by beneficial help.
lines.plainText: To seek thy health by beneficial help

lines.text: Try all the friends thou hast in Ephesus;
lines.plainText: Try all the friends thou hast in Ephesus

lines.text: Beg thou, or borrow, to make up the sum,
lines.plainText: Beg thou or borrow to make up the sum

lines.text: And live; if no, then thou art doom'd to die.
lines.plainText: And live if no then thou art doom'd to die

lines.text: Jailer, take him to thy custody.
lines.plainText: Jailer take him to thy custody

lines.text: I will, my lord.
lines.plainText: I will my lord

lines.text: Hopeless and helpless doth Egeon wend,
lines.plainText: Hopeless and helpless doth Egeon wend

lines.text: But to procrastinate his lifeless end.
lines.plainText: But to procrastinate his lifeless end
